correctness.rationale: On the specified three-state Potts–SOS Cayley tree branch r=theta², x=1, the printed boundary law reduces to F(theta,y)=y³-theta*y²+2theta*y-2=0 with y>0. The nontrivial eigenvalue quadratic has zero constant term and reduces to {0,rho}, rho=y(theta-y)/(2theta+y²). The binary-tree Kesten–Stigum equality 2rho²=1 gives polynomial K=2y²(theta-y)²-(2theta+y²)². Independent symbolic Sylvester resultant verifies Res_y(F,K)=16P(theta) for the stated octic. The exact rational Sturm argument in RESULT and verifier proves P has precisely two positive roots in disjoint rational intervals; over Q(sqrt2) its two quartic factors distinguish rho=-1/sqrt2 at theta_minus and rho=+1/sqrt2 at theta_plus. Substitution and sign brackets put the large crossing on the middle of three positive cubic branches. Independent numeric root/branch calculation agrees at 0.166699331094 and 9.706301627792; decimal checks do not prove global root count. This is the Kesten–Stigum sufficient non-extremality threshold only, not an exact extremality criterion.
risk: Numerical root checks are not a substitute for exact Sturm proof; octic resultant can have spurious algebraic roots without positive-real branch isolation, addressed by sign analysis.
Only r=theta², x=1 branch and binary tree Kesten–Stigum sufficient condition.
